speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the foreign domestic worker levy can be waived for families with three or more young children who are below 16 years of age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It is not sustainable for the population of FDWs to grow unchecked.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To moderate the demand for FDWs in Singapore, a levy has been payable by employers since April 1982.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This measure strikes a good balance between managing FDW demand and the need for continuing support for Singaporean households with children, seniors and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government also provides other forms of support for families with children, some of which offer even more assistance to larger families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Parents with more children are also eligible for higher tax rebates and reliefs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As was announced recently during the National Day Rally, preschool subsidies will also be substantially enhanced.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our latest total fertility rate (TFR) for 2018 shows a number of 1.14.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is the second lowest TFR in the past decade.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And given the heavy demands of work, many parents have found it to be a necessity to employ an FDW to help them to do household chores and look after their kids.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe The Straits Times ran an article over the weekend on this particular subject.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, will the Ministry consider waiving FDW levies for families with more than three children in order to help them lower their financial demands and to encourage them to have more than three children?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some of these parents with young children are also staying with their grandparents, so inter-generational households.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, inter-generational households may hire more than two FDWs with levy concessions, just to give an example.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, a couple with two young children under the age of 16 can hire two FDWs at the concessionary levy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And if their parents are staying with them and the parents are above 67, because that sometimes is the preferred arrangement – extended family – they will be entitled to hire an FDW at the concessionary levy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, in this example, the household would be able to hire three FDWs to help the parents, especially when they have young children, whether two, three or more.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If Mr Ong Teng Koon would allow me to elaborate, the Government has committed additional resources and investments in preschool education to give our young the best start in life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I am saying that when young couples consider having children or more children, an FDW could be one of the considerations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But more often than not, a preschool is also a key consideration.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And to help families with young children financially, the Government provides many forms of support.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition to those that I have mentioned, the Government also provides support, such as primary and secondary school subsidies as well as parental tax rebates and reliefs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: A child entering primary school in 2018 would have received more than $130,000 in education subsidies by the time he or she finishes secondary school.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And bigger families with more children will also receive more help from the Baby Bonus scheme as well as higher tax rebates.
